content.intro: Learn partitioning and ordering window results in the context of window functions and analytical queries. This lesson covers the supplied syllabus topic, demonstrates a representative MySQL example, and finishes with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Analytical queries define a row grain, compute metrics at that grain, and make ordering and tie behavior explicit. Aggregate queries collapse rows into groups; window functions calculate across related rows without collapsing the current row set.

content_blocks.title: Apply the idea
content_blocks.text: Calculate a small result by hand, run the grouped/windowed query, and check row grain, ties, and NULL behavior. Write down the expected result before running the snippet. Compare actual output with the reference, then try one normal case and one edge case.

content_blocks.code: WITH daily_sales AS (SELECT DATE('2026-10-10') AS sold_on, 10 AS amount UNION ALL SELECT DATE('2026-10-11'), 15 UNION ALL SELECT DATE('2026-10-12'), 20) SELECT sold_on, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sold_on ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total FROM daily_sales ORDER BY sold_on;
content_blocks.expected_output: Rows show running_total 10, 25, and 45. The explicit frame makes the intended running calculation visible.
